citations.locator: Lecture 17, physical PDF page 510, printed slide 6: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
Cartesian Straight-Line Motion
•  A common requirement is to move the tool frame along a straight-line path in
   Cartesian space. This is achieved by interpolating both position and orientation
   between the initial and final configurations.
•  The position of the tool frame is interpolated linearly between the initial and
    final points. The orientation is interpolated using the angle–axis representation,
   which provides a smooth rotational transition.
•  The path is divided into two regions:.
    – A linear region, where motion proceeds at constant
        velocity
    – Blend regions, where acceleration and deceleration occur
•  This leads to the formulation of motion using linear
   splines with parabolic blends, ensuring continuity of
   velocity and acceleration.

optionExplanations.o3: Slopes can be matched despite different polynomial degrees.
